title: Explaining Realized Returns: Roll's $R^2$ 40 Years Later
abstract: arXiv:2611.22277v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can we explain asset price movements even with hindsight? Reinterpreting Roll's (1988) AFA Presidential Address, "$R^2$," as a modern empirical exercise, we show that conventional macroeconomic, cash-flow, expectations, and flow variables explain less than 10% (often with negative $R^2$) of monthly U.S. equity return variation out of sample and lack daily observations. We use generative AI to extract reasons stated in Wall Street Journal market summaries while filtering out price-related language. These reasons explain around 30-40% of daily and monthly return variation out of sample. Their content spans interpretable themes, including corporate news, macroeconomic conditions, monetary policy, sentiment, and geopolitics.

translated_title: 解释已实现收益：罗尔的 R² 四十年后
translated_abstract: 即便事后回看，我们能否解释资产价格的变动？本文将罗尔（Roll, 1988）在美国金融学会（AFA）主席演讲《R²》重新解读为一项现代实证研究，结果显示：传统的宏观经济、现金流、预期以及资金流变量在样本外对美国股票月度收益率波动的解释力不足10%（且R²常为负值），并且这些变量缺乏日度观测数据。我们利用生成式人工智能从《华尔街日报》的市场综述中提取所陈述的原因，同时过滤掉与价格相关的语言。这些原因在样本外能够解释约30-40%的日度和月度收益率波动，其内容涵盖可解释的主题，包括公司新闻、宏观经济状况、货币政策、市场情绪和地缘政治。
tldr: 本文利用生成式AI从《华尔街日报》市场综述中提取剔除价格相关语言的原因文本，发现这些原因在样本外能解释约30-40%的股票收益率波动，远超传统宏观经济等变量不足10%的解释力，验证了四十年前罗尔提出的R²之谜在新时代的解答。
en_tdlr: Using generative AI to extract non-price-related reasons from Wall Street Journal market summaries, this paper shows these reasons explain 30-40% of out-of-sample daily and monthly equity return variation, far exceeding the less-than-10% explanatory power of conventional macroeconomic, cash-flow, expectations, and flow variables, resolving Roll's 40-year-old R² puzzle in a modern way.
